fixed.how: New tools/orchestration/wallclock.py: perf marks by AST (a test method that reads HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS via get / getenv / environ[...] / in, or calls wall_clock_bound), with the sha256 of each method's source; the committed registry gate_policy/perf_tests.json lists all 26 bounds (a new mark is visible in review: an unregistered one fails green_tests.py's correctness run, CI and the gate's G1); the relax plan. The gate's _unittest worker runs every perf-marked test of a correctness run (HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS=0) relaxed: HOUSE_SIM_PERF_TESTS=relaxed so the legacy guard lets the body run, under a counting clock (perf_counter / monotonic / process_time / time and _ns advance 1 us per call, also names the test module bound by import) so only functional assertions can fail; the new helper wall_clock_bound(self, elapsed, limit) asserts in the perf job and records (HOUSE_SIM_PERF_RECORD) otherwise. green_tests.py's correctness runs (CI) go through the worker; a perf-marked test that still skips with the bound message fails the run; G1 / G1b / G8 count it as a skip (a regression whatever the previous record ran) unless the registry gives it a dated skip exception pinned to its exact source (one: the thermal relative bound, until 2026-11-30); compare recomputes this from tests.json 'bounds'. 25 of the 26 bounds now run their bodies in the correctness suite (probed normal, strict and HOUSE_SIM_DOMAINS=core).
